title: John Armstrong to James Madison, coded postscript of 30 Aug 1808 (THE=972 code), Madison Papers LoC reel 10 frame 0521

steps.what: Took the 49-group postscript from Founders Online.
Loaded Tomokiyo's 227-entry partial table from the 4 May 1806 known-plaintext letter as the base layer.
Fetched NARA M34 roll 13 frames and ranked them for pencil with pencil_score.py to find clerk-decoded despatches.
Read the clerk's pencil decodes over the October 1806 despatch (frames 0192-0201) into pairs.txt (584 lines, H/M graded) and merged them with the base table.
First reading took the subject as 'S.' = Skipwith with 1394 a null.
Filled 12 groups by context checked against their alphabetical slot (1394 ru, 1273 el, 250 ought, 148 consul, 130 America, 720 bir, 992 qua, 1048 fi, 1202 above, 1052 fit, 384 Ward, 1483 ish).
Read the 22 Feb 1808 private letter in the same code with the merged table; it reads with gaps and fixes ru, ish and Russia.
Re-fetched roll 13 through the NARA catalogue proxy; frame 0190 gives 1320 = like and other H pairs.
Collated the groups against the LoC manuscript image: two Founders errors corrected, final 555 identified as a slip for 1555 man.
Postscript read: Russel ought to be the consul ... like Warden an Irish[man]; 48 of 49 groups determined.
Paired control: the 15 Feb 1808 despatch in THE=972 reads (176 of 243 groups H/C) while the 20 Feb 1808 letter gives noise (92 of 369 hits), so the latter is a different code.
Adjudicated the AFIO 2025 solution of the 20 Feb 1808 letter against a shuffled-ciphertext control (adjudicate_feb20.py); it fits worse than the control.
Reran the pencil score over all 393 roll-13 frames; it does not locate the annotated frames beyond the first page of a decoded despatch.

Crawled Founders Online's Armstrong-Madison chain through the Wayback Machine (founders_crawl.py, fo/), Sept 1807 - Feb 1809 early-access and the 1804-1811 published volumes; counted code runs per document.

Found that roll 14 (naId 188671566, Jan 1808 - Sept 1810) was already on disk in img/ (665 frames); paged all frames at 12 per sheet (grids14/) and located the long code runs: 0024-25 (15 Feb 1808), 0029-34 (20/22 Feb), 0476-77, 0494, 0495 (20 Jan, 2 Feb, 17 Feb 1810, with pencil decodes), 0643-44 (copy of 5 Mar 1808). Short runs (13 Aug, 30 Aug, 25 Oct 1808) were not visible at that scale.

Checked the Founders group lists of 15 Feb, 22 Feb and 5 Mar 1808 against frames 0024-25, 0034 and 0643; recorded 21 corrections in fix972.json (e.g. 22 Feb 1436->1456, 723 1357 755 -> 723 1337 255; 5 Mar 7->417, 1155->1165, 1150/893->1251/895, 1801->1201).
Transcribed the three 1810 despatches to Robert Smith (20 Jan, 2 Feb, 17 Feb 1810) from roll 14 frames 0476-77, 0494, 0495 with the State Department pencil interlinear (transcripts14.txt).

15 Feb 1808 read with the table plus context: hand, alliance, against, Great Britain (pencil 'G.B.'), if, war, kind, pick pockets, blessings, diligence, driven (pencil), trial, abandon, doctrine, well, come to blows, settlement, western boundary (pencil 'Boundary'); 1105 = comma, 962 = full stop, 1104/897 = semicolon. 243 of 243 groups given a value.

22 Feb 1808 extended: Gustavus (946 as Gu by context), old course, completely, humiliation, Bonaparte disdain to wear the crown, whose wealth, colonies, ally/enemy, true policy, threshold, altogether, American interest, Darien, common defence, restricted to Cuba and Mexico, league, commenced by Cretet seconded by Fouché supported by Talleyrand. 380 of 387 given a value.

608 is u/v, not 'va' alone: Gusta-v-us, Fo-u-ch-é, excl-u-de, fra-u-d (17 Feb 1810 pencil 'fraud'), act-u-al-ly; 773 = ea (sp-ea-k, 5 Mar) so the first Bonaparte in 22 Feb (773) is a slip for 723 bo, written correctly four lines later.

5/9 Mar 1808 (Armstrong's 5 Mar note to Lafayette and Lafayette's Friday reply, plus 9 Mar): Champagny, the jurisdiction of the judicial department sent to the grand juge, little encouragement, transmitted to Talleyrand, had not the opportunity, tomorrow, perhaps, indulge, Cretet, obscure and a little contradictory, exception to the operation of the November decree. 385 of 408 given a value.

27/29 Dec 1807, 13 Aug, 25 Oct, 26 Mar, 31 May, 6 Jun 1808 decoded with the extended table; 1810 despatches read with their pencil decodes (turn, negociation, duke of Cadore; Mr Petry, convention, reciprocal advantage; to justify the violence already committed on our commerce ... neither hasty nor uncharitable ... force or fraud).

Conflicts kept open rather than forced: 1260 = dou (22 Feb 1808) vs chari (17 Feb 1810 triplicate); 720 = bir (PS inference) vs 'da' needed in bri-ga-n-?-ge (26 Mar 1808); 396 = while vs pencil 'which' (17 Feb 1810); 1415 = be (C) and ble (pencil 'blessings').

Measured per-despatch share with despatches.py (shares.txt): H/C-known 64-79%; with M, inferred and this session's 160 additions: 15 Feb 100%, 22 Feb 98.2%, 5 Mar 94.4%, 27 Dec 89.3%, 13 Aug 92.6%, 25 Oct 90.9%, 1810 three 100%. The additions are context inferences ('?') checked against slot order, not independent confirmations.

The 1804-1807 despatches are printed decoded (italics) in the published Secretary of State Series from clerks' decodes or the editors' partial key; no group lists, so they were inventoried but not re-read group by group.

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The 1808 postscript (LoC Madison Papers) was read from a codebook rebuilt out of a State Department clerk's pencil decodes over Armstrong's 1806-07 despatches on NARA microfilm M34 roll 13, merged with Tomokiyo's partial table from the 4 May 1806 known-plaintext letter, with the remaining groups inferred from their alphabetical slot.
outcome.fraction_read_source: python decode972.py ps: 49 of 49 cipher tokens given a value (the last, 555, only by emendation to 1555)
outcome.notes: 48 of 49 groups read as sense (fraction_coherent 48/49); the 49th is a probable slip. By distinct group in NOTES: 29 H/C (pencil decodes or Tomokiyo's known plaintext, including 1320 like), 12 slot-inferred, 555 emended; decode972.py marks ?/* but does not separate H from C, so grades are not counted. The first commit (2026-09-14) carries no model trailer; later ones Claude Fable 5.1. 2026-10-02: the table was extended (additions972.tsv, ~160 context values) and applied to 13 further despatches/runs of 1807-1810 (despatches.py, inventory.tsv); the profile outcome still describes the 30 Aug 1808 postscript.

prior.where: Tomokiyo's partial table from the 4 May 1806 known-plaintext letter (about a third of the postscript groups; code972_partial.json, 227 entries). No full reading of the postscript found in archive, print or online.

human: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5 and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. The LoC image, blocked to scripts, was collated by hand; the NOTES do not say by whom.
